gloss: to face each other, to confront

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {向|む}き{合|あ}いませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {向|む}き{合|あ}っていなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {向|む}き{合|あ}っていませんでした

definitions.explanation: To be positioned facing one another.
To face a problem, challenge, or difficult situation directly (figurative use).

examples.japanese: ⟦{二人|ふたり}→二人：00622_futari⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{向|む}き{合|あ}って⟦{座|すわ}った→座る：00757_suwaru⟧。
examples.english: The two sat facing each other.

examples.japanese: ⟦{鏡|かがみ}→鏡：02190_kagami⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{向|む}き{合|あ}う。
⟦テーブル→テーブル：04488_teeburu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{挟|はさ}んで→挟む：00091_hasamu⟧{向|む}き{合|あ}って⟦{話|はな}した→話す：00467_hanasu⟧。
examples.english: We talked facing each other across the table.

examples.japanese: ⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{真剣|しんけん}に→真剣：01565_shinken⟧{向|む}き{合|あ}う⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: We need to seriously confront the problem.

examples.japanese: ⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{向|む}き{合|あ}う⟦{時間|じかん}→時間：00468_jikan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{欲|ほ}しい→欲しい：01107_hoshii⟧。
examples.english: I want time to face myself.

examples.japanese: ⟦{現実|げんじつ}→現実：02720_genjitsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{向|む}き{合|あ}わなければ、⟦{何|なに}も→何も：03874_nanimo⟧⟦{変|か}わらない→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧。
examples.english: If you don't face reality, nothing will change.

notes:
{向|む}き{合|あ}う is an intransitive verb (⟦{自動詞|じどうし}→自動詞：10977_jidoushi⟧) meaning to face each other or confront.

ETYMOLOGY:
- ⟦{向|む}く→向く：02304_muku⟧ (to face) + ⟦{合|あ}う→合う：10466_au⟧ (each other) → to face each other

ASPECT (ている):
{向|む}き{合|あ}っている indicates a state of facing each other or confronting something.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ⟦{互|たが}いに→互いに：07150_tagaini⟧{向|む}き{合|あ}う (face each other mutually)
- ⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{向|む}き{合|あ}う (confront a problem)
- ⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{向|む}き{合|あ}う (face oneself, reflect)
- ⟦{真剣|しんけん}→真剣：01565_shinken⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{向|む}き{合|あ}う (face seriously)

USAGE:
Commonly used in the figurative sense of dealing with or confronting problems, challenges, or oneself. Very common in self-help and psychological contexts.
